summary: Adoption is deep and the executive sponsor is engaged, but there is no pre-launch baseline and no outcome measured in claims terms. The sponsor faces a CFO line-by-line review in about 60 days and a cheaper bundled alternative from the core claims vendor.

indicators.evidence: SVP of Claims requested the review, set the agenda, and committed to unblock IT and finance.
indicators.quote: I can push the IT request. I'll talk to the CIO's chief of staff this week.

indicators.evidence: Customer describes user satisfaction and dependence, not business value.
indicators.quote: I had a feeling, but I didn't have an answer.

indicators.evidence: SVP and Director engaged; IT data owners, finance, and the CFO are not.
indicators.quote: IT does. Specifically a team under the CIO. They're not unfriendly, they're just buried.

indicators.evidence: No sponsor turnover mentioned. The sponsor is under budget pressure but in role. A reporting analyst left in the spring.
Original business case named cycle time and manual touches; the sponsor now needs cost per claim and adjuster capacity, which were never defined as targets.
indicators.quote: Something on cost per claim or adjuster capacity, because that's how he thinks.

indicators.evidence: No clean pre-launch baseline exists for cycle time.
indicators.quote: We don't have a clean before.

indicators.evidence: Reports describe platform activity, not claims outcomes. Subrogation impact is anecdotal.
indicators.quote: The reports we get from your platform are about the platform.

indicators.evidence: The sponsor could not answer the CFO's question about what the spend delivered.
indicators.quote: what did we get for the six hundred and eighty thousand we spend on Fieldstone. And I didn't have a good answer.
We've got roughly eleven hundred adjusters on it.

indicators.evidence: 34 workflows in production, including FNOL routing on every new auto and property claim.
indicators.quote: If we turned it off tomorrow there would be a riot on the floor.

indicators.evidence: No adoption blockers raised. The blockers are on measurement, not usage.
Sponsor drives the meeting, names three required outputs, and discloses competitive pressure.
indicators.quote: Three things. A before and after on cycle time for at least one line of business.

indicators.evidence: Commercial lines wants the platform, but the sponsor is holding expansion until value is proven.
indicators.quote: I'm not expanding something I can't defend.

indicators.evidence: Neither the sponsor nor finance can attribute any outcome to the investment yet.
indicators.quote: I need it to come from our data, not your marketing slides.

maturity.rationale: Core workflows are embedded across the claims floor, but no outcomes are measured against a baseline. Reaching Realizing Value requires a defensible before-and-after in claims terms from Crestview data.

kpis.note: Baseline lost when the analyst who owned the dashboard left.

kpis.current: Recovery team reports more referrals; count unknown

useCases.evidence: Running daily; recovery team reports more referrals.

risks.text: CFO line-by-line review in about 60 days with no defensible value story.
Core claims vendor is offering a cheaper bundle claimed to cover 80% of the capability.
Historical data extract has been stuck in the IT queue since July.
Vendor reporting is platform-centric, so the customer cannot translate it to claims outcomes.

opportunities.text: Subrogation recoveries may be the fastest outcome to prove.
Commercial lines expansion once value is defensible.
Sponsor is willing to unblock IT and finance personally.

actions.action: Run a four-week value assessment in claims terms
actions.detail: Deliver the three outputs the sponsor named: a before-and-after on cycle time for one line of business, a cost per claim or capacity view, and a page sourced from Crestview data.
actions.timeframe: Start this week; finish within 4 weeks

actions.detail: Sponsor escalates to the CIO's chief of staff; agree a partial extract if a full one cannot land in time.
Pull the recovery team's referral data before and after go-live and agree a value per recovery with finance.
One hour with finance to use their cost per claim method, so the CFO sees his own numbers.

actions.action: Replace platform reports with claims-outcome reporting
actions.detail: Redesign the monthly report around cycle time, touches, and recoveries instead of workflow volumes.

actions.action: Prepare a competitive position against the bundle
actions.detail: Document what the bundled alternative would not cover, grounded in Crestview's 34 production workflows.

statedFacts: About 1,100 adjusters use the platform, roughly 85% weekly active.
34 automated workflows are in production, including FNOL routing on every new auto and property claim.
No pre-launch cycle time baseline exists; current auto physical damage cycle time is roughly 11 days by recollection.
valueNarrative.draft: Crestview's adjusters rely on Fieldstone every day: about 1,100 users, 34 workflows in production, and FNOL routing on every new claim. What we cannot yet show is what that has done to cycle time, touches, or cost per claim, because the pre-launch baseline was lost. Over the next four weeks we will rebuild a before-and-after from Crestview's own claims data, starting with subrogation recoveries.
caveats: No outcome figures are shown until a baseline is rebuilt from Crestview data.
The 11-day cycle time is an estimate, not a measured value.

projection.text: If nothing changes, Crestview enters the CFO review without a defensible number and the cheaper bundle becomes the default, putting the March renewal at serious risk despite strong usage.
